text:
Alex W: Heads up — observed weird kernel swap pattern on nightly that causes allocator pressure and intermittent OOMs on p4d-prod.
Maria G: Can you paste the perf trace? nvprof/nvtx or nsight?
Alex W: Pasted a short sample:
```
[NSIGHT] kernel: flash_attn_forward  mem: 11.2GiB time: 5.8ms
[NSIGHT] kernel: triton_attn_fwd    mem: 13.7GiB time: 6.1ms
[NSIGHT] kernel: ffn_cublasLt_gemm  mem: 9.6GiB  time: 4.3ms
CUDA pool high watermark: 14.8GiB
allocator fragmentation: 1.8GiB
KV cache active: 6.1GiB
```
Samir P: looks like flash attention wins latency but pushes mem high due to workspace peaks for long seqs. what batch/seq mix was this?
Alex W: Mixed: 40% seq=2048, 50% seq=512, 10% seq=64; average token per request 740. Batching turned on with dynamic window of 8.
Maria G: Our current workspace heuristic sizes flash/workspace = max(seq)*head_dim*scale then pad to 256KiB. That's too naive for skewed distribution.
Joan L: Agree. When a single long request triggers flash kernel it reserves big workspace and blocks subsequent reuse => swap/evict. We need a cheaper fallback for percentile-based sizing.
perf-bot: Regression alert: nightly 1784060000 shows +18% OOM events on p4d-prod compared to last week.
Samir P: Proposal: use 95th-percentile seq for workspace sizing per-minute instead of max, with an escape hatch: if allocating would exceed pool_threshold then pick Triton kernel or cuBLASLt FFN which uses smaller temp buffers.
Alex W: Microbench: switching to triton for seq>1536 reduces peak mem by ~1.6GiB but adds 0.3ms median latency on those requests.
Maria G: Also try cooperative buffer reuse: allow KV cache buffers to be reclaimed for temporary workspace during generation of short-lived logits compute, with a pin/unpin protocol.
Joan L: Risky for privacy but acceptable if we only reclaim zeroed and pinned buffers when KV not accessed for >2s and under 1% tail load. Need audit/logging.
Samir P: Implementation plan:
- metric: p95_seq, pool_high_watermark
- heuristic: if alloc_request + pool_used > pool_cap * 0.92 => choose smaller-kernel fallback
- implement buffer loaning API: loan(buffer_id, purpose, timeout)
- add perf tests and canary on dedicated cluster
Alex W: I'll prototype kernel-choice shim in runtime. Patch will log decisions via nvtx: `RT:kernel-choice flash->triton reason=mem-pressure`
perf-bot: New job queued: perf/bench/kernel-choice-shim #342
Maria G: One more idea: quantize workspace buffers for FFN matmul (fp16 workspace) if model supports. Cuts workspace ~25% in my tests.
Joan L: Action: Alex prototyping, Samir to add metric hooks, Maria to run microbench on quant workspace, I'll own canary rollout. Target: PR by EOD Friday.
Alex W: Will post first draft patch and a small perf table.
Maria G: Thanks — also add a flag to force old heuristic for quick rollback.
Samir P: Noted. cc @ops for capacity planning.
Alex W: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
